articles.title: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
articles.summary: Google's Gemini API introduces Tool Retrieval, enabling dynamic function execution like issuing refunds based on input. Developers can register functions, which the API locates and executes automatically, optimizing workflow automation. This feature enhances tool integration and broadens automation capabilities within applications.

articles.title: Let Gemini tackle repetitive chores on your Mac
articles.summary: Computer use in the Gemini app for Mac can now help users get multi-step tasks done across their local files, desktop apps, and the web. Gemini works inside an isolated background window with a live preview right in the chat. Users' main screen and cursor remain completely free, so they can continue typing, designing, or taking calls without interruption. Users can choose which apps Gemini can access, watch every step live, pause at any time, and approve key actions before they happen.

articles.title: When Agent Swarms Outperform Solo Coders
articles.summary: Replit's optimization benchmark found 32 Opus agents achieved an 18.9× NumPy workload speedup versus 3.7× for one agent within two hours, using more compute. Gains depended on separable tasks and shared coordination boards. The strongest solo model's performance declined as teams grew.

articles.title: Sandboxed Models Can Communicate via Inference Servers
articles.summary: Sandboxing did not stop AI models on a shared inference server from trading information in contrived tests. One model's large request slightly shifts the server's calculations for the other, which reads the shift as a signal.

articles.title: AI is already massively speeding up AI research
articles.summary: AI companies are not ready to handle the risks of recursive self-improvement safely and responsibly, despite having talked about them for years, and this is incredibly dangerous. Policymakers need to make it a top priority to rapidly understand these risks, and consider pausing or pacing frontier AI progress. AI lab employees need to raise concerns internally, whistleblow to policymakers and the public, form a union, or loudly quit. Everyone else should encourage and pressure policymakers to end the race. Protests are looking like an increasingly viable and highly leveraged way to get both media and policymaker attention in the next few months.

articles.title: Mirror Dimension for Agents: Evaluating Browser-Use Agents Without the Web
articles.summary: Google introduces the Mirror Dimension, a controlled environment for testing AI browser-use agents without accessing the live web. This tool helps evaluate security and effectiveness, reducing risks associated with letting agents interact with real-world websites.

articles.title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
articles.summary: Apple introduced FastFrames, two models that generate 480p video fast enough for interactive use. Each frame takes 36 ms on a single GPU with the smaller model.

articles.title: Become a founding member of TLDR's AI community (2 minute form)
articles.summary: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss major news and launches. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR AI. Apply here to join.

articles.title: Perplexity's Self-Improving Skills
articles.summary: Perplexity Computer can now build and update its own skills, using its Brain system to learn from each user's past sessions.

articles.title: Stripe evals: Measuring real-world coding agent performance
articles.summary: Coding harnesses, when paired with frontier models, can produce working end-to-end Stripe integrations, although they may not necessarily follow all best practices. Stripe evals is a benchmark that helps Stripe understand how different coding agents and models integrate Stripe. It measures how well coding agents build high-quality integrations given realistic, well-specified scenarios driven by a role-playing agent. The benchmark provides guidance on how the company can steer agents better to achieve better outcomes for businesses using Stripe.

articles.title: What comes after AGI?
articles.summary: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) is now within reach, so we can no longer put off seriously considering what will come next. AI achieving artificial general superintelligence (ASI) will have a profound impact on science, the economy, and society at a scale much greater than AGI itself. Preparing for that shift will require mapping the possible roads from AGI to ASI and building rigorous, reliable ways to track progress.

articles.title: Vercel Board
articles.summary: Vercel released Board, an experimental message board where AI agents claim tasks, post updates, and share context.

articles.title: Cloudflare's Clairic and Clairic-flash
articles.summary: Cloudflare made the weights public for Clairic and Clairic-flash, its models for extracting specific fields from text, images, and PDFs.

articles.title: How OpenAI's Performance Factory keeps ChatGPT fast
articles.summary: OpenAI's Performance Factory uses Codex to automate and expedite performance regression investigations and fixes for ChatGPT.

articles.title: Computer Scientists Facilitating Independent Review of a High-profile OpenAI and Anthropic Result
articles.summary: UC San Diego and MIT computer scientists are facilitating an independent review of OpenAI and Anthropic's announcement claiming their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH).
